metadata.title: A Structure-First Approach to Research Reading
metadata.indexTerms: Document structure · scholarly reading · citation links

blocks.text: Research papers are built for print, but research reading happens across screens, notes, and linked evidence. We present a structure-first reading model that turns a paper into a navigable workspace while preserving its scholarly relationships.

Reading a paper is rarely a linear act. A reader moves between the claim in front of them, the figure that supports it, and the prior work behind a citation. Existing PDF viewers preserve the page, but leave these relationships hidden in the visual surface [12].

Our approach treats the paper as a structured document rather than a page image. The representation separates content, layout, and scholarly links, allowing each layer to be rendered for the task at hand.
When a reader follows [15], the useful next step is a compact view of the referenced work: title, authors, venue, and a path back to the bibliography.

items: A normalized document model independent of the extraction engine.
A reader that connects sections, figures, tables, and references.
A graceful path from local PDF text extraction to richer parsing.

blocks.text: We combine layout-aware extraction with citation parsing. Blocks become typed nodes—paragraphs, figures, tables, equations, and citations—then a renderer composes them into an accessible reading surface.

blocks.text: The reader is organized around section navigation, continuous reading progress, and reference lookup. Uploaded PDFs use local text extraction and may not preserve every complex layout.

A stable document model lets the interface evolve independently from the parser. Figures, tables, equations, and citation links belong in the document model so the reader can present them as native web content.
